nodes.evidence: YAML parsed and CPU stressor extracted
runtime CPU, latency, error and restart metrics required; not present in static source
restart/recovery behavior is deployment/runtime dependent and pending

test_value_hypothesis.reason: The stressor is materially above the declared 200m CPU limit and can test whether readiness, latency and error behavior reveal resource pressure.
test_value_hypothesis.boundary: CPU saturation can affect every endpoint on the selected pod; use one low-rate read-only request workload and a short duration.
test_value_hypothesis.safe_first_injection: Capture pod CPU/throttling, readiness, latency and error baselines before applying; start with one worker and a short duration, then increase only if metrics are available.

defense_hypotheses.hypothesis: The container CPU limit should contain usage, but throttling may increase request latency before readiness becomes false.
defense_hypotheses.static_support: Deployment declares requests.cpu=50m and limits.cpu=200m; runtime throttling is not observable from source.

defense_hypotheses.hypothesis: A TCP readiness probe can remain healthy while application-level latency or errors degrade.
defense_hypotheses.static_support: The readiness probe only checks TCP connectivity on port 12031.

result_classification_rules: If CPU throttling rises, readiness remains true, and request latency/error SLO degrades: classify as partial resource defense with an observability gap.
If the pod is evicted/restarted and recovers within the declared budget: classify recovery separately from request-level defense.
If no CPU pressure or business effect is observed, first verify the stress injector matched the intended pod before classifying as defended.
A successful StressChaos record proves the test node was injected; it does not prove CPU saturation without direct CPU/throttling metrics.
next_evidence: Exercise a reachable order workflow that performs a real downstream call, not only a local not-found lookup.
Keep cgroup counters, request latency, readiness events and application logs on one timestamped timeline.
Run the original five-minute profile only after a human-approved stop budget and a business-path oracle are defined.

runtime_evidence.runtime_lesson: The stronger short profile and the selector-generated replay both produced measurable cgroup throttling while preserving the tested response contract and Pod recovery. The defense conclusion remains bounded by duration, endpoint and workload.
runtime_evidence.generated_profile_lesson: A candidate produced from the test-node selection pipeline reached the intended cgroup only after injectedCount=1, measured throttling, preserved the exercised read-only response, and recovered without restart. This validates the selector-to-runner path, not universal service defense.
